title: Draft: Qt: Add signal for columnHeadersChanged
description:
Add a new signal for columnHeadersChanged to avoid updating column
data when not needed. Use this signal at startup, when changing
profile and when closing the preferences dialog. Here the packets
will be dissected or redissected later.

Freeze the packet list early when changing profile and when closing
the preferences dialog to avoid showing inconsistent column data
before redissecting packets. The packet list will be thawed when
redissection is done.

notes.body: mentioned in issue #19079

The disadvantage of this solution is that the packet list data are out of sync with the headers for a short period until the redissect happens. This doesn't happen without this changes because both the data and headers are updated (using old conversations etc.) before the redissect happens.

added 11 commits
  • 52babf2e...aa6b8368 - 10 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 9780268b - Qt: Add signal for columnHeadersChanged
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10716/diffs?diff_id=686756277&start_sha=52babf2eb70f4b7aa22f704c472c8916b95b6e21)

In my testing, it does seem to prevent the issue where the data is dissected with new preferences but old conversations / file scoped packet data, etc. It's a little difficult for me to see the effect of the packet list data being out of sync with the headers, since the redissect happens quickly.

Are there any possible downsides of that? It doesn't seem as bad as the problem of dissecting with preferences inconsistent with current file scoped data from other frames.

I usually just see the packet list flickering, and I use Screen Recording to see what's actually happening. Try switching between profiles with a lot of different columns and slowly playback a recording.

I'm looking at an alternative solution with packet list `clear()` before doing `resetColumns()`. This should have the same effect on redissect, and will also avoid showing data out of sync with the headers. The only issue here is to restore the selected frame. I'll create a new Draft PR if I manage to make something working.

mentioned in merge request !10822
This changes still have the issue of not selecting the previously selected packet when done.

`selectionChanged()` gets called a few times with things frozen and no model, which then always ends up calling `cf_unselect_packet()`, which clears `cf->current_frame`.

`rescan_packets()` reads `cf->current_frame` to try to see if it the current frame is still displayed after redissecting.

The `thaw()` that gets called from redissection doesn't try to restore selection, because `rescan_packets()` sometimes changes what packets are displayed. It does, however, clear the list of stored frozen rows.

Since `cf->current_frame` was NULL when entering `rescan_packets`, it doesn't find any row matching the current frame, and the first row ends up being selected.

It also seems like this breaks sorting of columns that depend on frame data if `build_column_format_array()` has not been called yet. If I sort on a column like Protocol or Info before anything that triggers ColumnHeadersChanged, I get lots of:

```file C:\Development\wireshark\epan\frame_data.c: line 151 (frame_data_compare): should not be reached```

and sorting doesn't work. It works fine after any change that causes `build_column_format_array()` to be called, including adding a column, etc.
I can remove the `build_column_format_array()` removal part, looks like it's still needed.

The capture in #18648 has a variety of the problem originally seen with TCP out of order; if the preference to "Call subdissector for retransmitted frames" is initially enabled and then disabled (through the preference dialog, not the context menu), then there's a redissection with a hash table not created. It doesn't crash, only a:

`[GLib CRITICAL] -- g_hash_table_lookup: assertion 'hash_table != NULL' failed`

console warning.
This changes fixes that.
I don't like the current state of this MR, but I will continue work on it when I have time. Hopefully I can find a better solution.

No better solution, but keeping the selected packet is fixed.
Maybe this changes is the best we can do for now.
